title: E-commerce Customer Segmentation
text:
Olist is a Brazilian e-commerce platform that connects small and medium-sized businesses to customers across Brazil. The platform operates as a marketplace, where merchants can list their products and services and customers can browse and purchase them online. Olist has rich e-commerce operational data, providing details at each stage of e-commerce sales.


Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce
The data was provided by Olist, containing multiple datasets that can be joined on certain keys. The schema is shown below:




The primary objective of our project is to conduct a comprehensive customer analysis for Olist. By diving deep into the behavioral patterns, transactional data, and overall engagement of customers, we aim to derive actionable insights that can drive personalized marketing strategies, enhance customer retention, and optimize resource allocation. The ultimate goal is to provide business intelligence that will empower the platform to not only meet but exceed customer expectations, thereby fostering a loyal customer base and driving sustainable growth.
The motivation behind choosing this particular topic stems from the recognition of customers as the lifeblood of any e-commerce platform. In today’s highly competitive digital marketplace, understanding customer behavior and value is vital and paramount. We were particularly drawn to the challenge of unlocking the potential within customer data, mainly in three aspects:
* Customer EDA: By exploring and understanding the underlying patterns in customer behaviors, we can provide a general overview of the Olist e-commerce data and uncover areas of improvement within the platform, primarily based on customer geolocation distribution and customer purchase preference.
* Customer Segmentation: By segmenting customers into meaningful groups based on their transactional behavior, we can enable targeted marketing efforts and more efficient allocation of resources, improving personalized customer experience. * Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) Prediction: Predicting LTV is crucial for decision-making about customer acquisition and retention strategies by focusing on customers who are most likely to contribute significantly to the platform’s profitability over time. 
To sum up, this project is driven by the desire to derive data-driven solutions that enable the e-commerce platform to not only survive but thrive in the competitive landscape. Through this analysis, we hope to contribute to the development of a more customer-centered platform that values and leverages the power of its customer data to drive decisions and strategies.

Experience

Data Science Intern | Penske Truck Leasing Co.
Reading, PA | May 2024 – July 2024

Participated in designed and deploying the key components of customer analytics platform supported with big data (1MM+ transaction records) in SAS and Python by combing RFM analysis with K-mean clustering and ML-based churn prediction to fulfill business requirements of model centralization and improve accuracy of personalized marketing strategies (20% higher retention rate).
Validated platform enhancements and data ingestions weekly, collaborating with senior analysts to compile performance reports.
Teamed with senior scientists to automate a data monitoring process in Python for Penske data warehouse and develop a web-based visualization tool for business teams to identify and override/correct +15 types of data anomalies including inconsistent data types, outliers, improper data proxy usage, and feeding issues of upstream data sources.
Provided strategic deliveries and remediation plans for self-identified data issues or ad hoc business requirements.
Maintained the memory allocation for all Spark jobs and coordinated across end users for production releases; monitored the cluster/queue usage and run log of daily batches.



E-commerce Customer Segementation

Conducted data preprocessing and feature engineering on 400K+ e-commerce transactions data to analyze customer purchase behaviors.
Extracted product categories from text descriptions using Python NLTK and clustered products into 5 distinct groups, leveraging WordCloud visualization for category identification.
Led customer segmentation analysis using PCA and K-means clustering based on their product preference and purchasing power features, and labeled customers into 11 segments based on morphology plots.
Developed a multi-classification model using XGBoost that can predict customer segments from their current purchase behaviors, addressed class imbalance using SMOTE, achieving accuracy over 85%.
Enabled targeted marketing and personalized engagement strategies by identifying customer segments and predicting future purchase patterns, enhancing customer experience and increasing sales potential.




Research Assistant | Virginia Tech
Blacksburg, VA | June 2022 - May 2023

Collaborated with an interdisciplinary research team from the Statistics Dept. and School of Plant and Environmental Sciences to develop AI-driven monitoring techniques for detecting subtle plant phenotype changes under stress conditions.
Implemented advanced data wrangling techniques in R (e.g., dplyr, ggplot2) to clean, process, and visualize plant health data across 100+ Excel datasets, ensuring accurate representation of monitoring proxies.
Developed and trained standalone ARIMA models for individual plants in treatment and control groups, applying F-tests on model parameters to identify statistically significant movement discrepancies. Results contributed to understanding plant stress responses.
Implemented and evaluated anomaly detection algorithms (moving average, Z-score, classification models) on multivariate time series data from six plant batches, improving detection of stimulus-driven movements and refining plant stress monitoring techniques.



Teaching Assistant | Virginia Tech
Blacksburg, VA | Jan 2023 - May 2023

Led weekly discussion sessions and recitations, guiding students through ordinary differential equations, stochastic modeling, and numerical methods, while developing supplementary materials, including practice problems and coding exercises in Python, to reinforce key concepts.
Graded assignments and exams, providing detailed feedback to enhance students’ understanding of numerical linear algebra, eigenvalue problems, and parameter estimation, while holding regular office hours to offer one-on-one support.
